name: Eich Well
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-05 (session 2) via NDWR WellLogQuery, owner search 'EICH': single exact match 'EICH, PAUL', Basin 087, T18N R20E Sec 21 SW, log 10437, completed 1969-01-25, depth 100 ft. Preferred over several superficially similar surnames in the same result set (Heidenreich, Eichelberger, Eichmann, Reichman, Reichlin, Meich) because this is the only literal 'Eich' owner in the area, and it sits ~403m from the separately-resolved DeMonte well and ~885m from Herz Domestic -- consistent with Klein et al. (2007) Figure 1's tight NDOT/Curti/Herz/DiMonte/Eich monitor-well cluster just N of the geothermal field. Minor caveat, not fully resolved: this log's total depth (100 ft) doesn't exactly match the NDEP permit table's description 'Eich (Shallow, 45 ft.)' -- plausibly a difference between total drilled depth and a specific sampling/perforation depth used for monitoring, rather than a wrong-well match.

STILL UNRESOLVED as of 2026-09-05 (session 2): searched NDWR WellLogQuery by owner name 'NDOT' -- got 24 statewide hits, but none plausibly close to the Klein et al. (2007) monitor-well cluster (~39.39-39.41N, -119.74 to -119.75W). The two Basin-087 candidates found were a 7-log cluster at T19N R19E Sec36 (39.4716,-119.7899, ~7-8km N of the cluster) and a single 'NDOT RIGHT OF WAY' log at T17N R20E Sec23 (39.317972,-119.707695, ~6-7km S/E) -- both rejected as too far away. Klein's map places NDOT immediately beside Curti/Herz/Soccer Field, so the true well is either logged under a different owner name (e.g. the actual maintenance-station name, or 'State of Nevada'/'Department of Transportation' rather than the abbreviation 'NDOT'), or simply isn't captured by an owner-name search at all. Left unlocated -- a spatial (GIS/map-based) NDWR search of the cluster area, rather than further owner-name guesses, is the more promising next step. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (session 33): a real candidate found while spot-checking well-log OCR for the Leapfrog/lithology task -- NDWR log 104216 (a WELL DRILLER'S PLUGGING REPORT) is owned by 'N.D.O.T.' (with periods -- explaining why the earlier owner-name search for the bare abbreviation 'NDOT' missed it), at address '1-580 Right of Way', with a precise NAD83 coordinate printed directly on the form: 39.37058 N, -119.75698 W (depth drilled 1990 ft, cased 1967 ft, references an earlier NDWR log #21768 as the original/replaced well). This coordinate sits ~2.2-4.4 km SOUTH of the Klein-map cluster this note originally expected, so it is flagged as a strong lead (exact owner-name + coordinate on a primary-source government form), NOT a confirmed match -- not registered as a Location/Well yet, per this project's standing rule against guessing an identity from a single lead without corroboration. Worth checking against Klein (2007)'s actual figure again (is NDOT really plotted at the Curti/Herz cluster, or was this note's summary of that figure imprecise?) before promoting. CORRECTION (same session, minutes later): rendered Klein et al. (2007) Figure 1 directly (output/figures/literature_reference/klein2007_fig1_wellmap.png) and can now see NDOT's real plotted position with certainty -- it IS in the northern Herz/Curti Barn/Curti Dom/Soccer Field/Brown School cluster (~39.39-39.41N), confirming this note's ORIGINAL expectation. Log 104216 (39.37058N, ~2.5km south) is therefore most likely a DIFFERENT N.D.O.T.-owned well (NDOT may own more than one monitoring well along area highways), not the Klein-mapped one. Still worth keeping on file as a real, confirmed N.D.O.T. identity (useful for other purposes), but downgraded from 'candidate lead for THIS location' to 'a different real NDOT well, doesn't resolve this row.'
